Prevention: Use only thrips-free seedlings from certified nurseries.
Control weeds in and around the fields to reduce thrips population.
UV-reflective mulches to disrupt host location by the thrips.
Plant early so that crops are well established and able to withstand thrips infestation.
Avoid intercropping tomato with host crops of thrips, e.g. capsicum, onion, nightshade, egg plant, irish potato etc.
Preserve natural enemies e.g. predatory mites, bugs, lacewings and ladybirds by planting flowering plants along borders and by avoiding broad-spectrum pesticides in the crop.
Apply balanced crop nutrition and avoid overuse of nitrogen.
Monitoring: Use blue or yellow sticky traps (one per acre) to check for presence of thrips in your field.
Look for tiny slender brownish insects on leaves & flowers by shaking them on a white piece of paper.
Look for deformation, speckling, or small necrotic patches on the surface of the attacked fruit.
Flowers and bud abortion may occur in heavy infestations.
Take action when 4-6 adults are seen per flower.
Direct Control: Uproot and destroy heavily infested plant/ plant parts.
Introduce predatory mites ( Amblyseius cucumeris ) when infestation is high.
Restrictions: Follow the instructions on the product label (Dosage, PHI, REI).
U (unlikely to present an acute hazard in normal use).
